claims.text: Designed and built the exception-handling engine end-to-end for Voltrix's multi-agent freight ops platform (planner/executor/reviewer pattern), cutting manual exception review time by 40%.
Owned prompt design and model routing across GPT-4 and open-weight SLMs, reducing inference cost by ~30%.
Sole architect of the retry/escalation logic now running in production, handling 5,000+ freight exceptions/month.
Presented the system design at a company-wide tech talk.
Built a RAG pipeline over carrier rate documents using LangChain + Pinecone, cutting manual rate lookup time significantly.
Improved BOL/invoice extraction accuracy through better OCR pre-processing.
Built Python microservices for a SaaS analytics product used by 50+ enterprise clients.
Led a 4-person team migrating a legacy monolith to microservices.

technical_qa.question: Walk me through the exception-handling engine you built at Voltrix.
technical_qa.answer: It's planner-executor-reviewer. Failures come in, get classified, retried or escalated, then double-checked. I designed the whole retry/escalation logic.

technical_qa.question: What made you choose that structure over a simpler rule-based system?
technical_qa.answer: Rules don't scale. Too many failure types — timeouts, bad EDI, missing BOL fields. Agents handle that better.

technical_qa.topic: Reviewer agent evaluation and verification metrics
technical_qa.question: How do you measure whether the reviewer agent is actually catching real problems?
technical_qa.answer: We track override rate. It's low. I'd have to check the exact number though, haven't looked recently.

technical_qa.topic: Model routing and cost optimization approach
technical_qa.question: What's your approach to model routing?
technical_qa.answer: Cost-based. Simple stuff to the SLM, harder reasoning to GPT-4. No formal study, just tuned it as things broke.

behavioral.friction_event_quote: Teammate wanted to hardcode more categories up front. I pushed for the agent approach. We went with mine.
behavioral.skeptic_followup_quote: Fine — 'sole architect' is probably too strong. I led the design, she built most of the production version.
behavioral.friction_notes: Conceded under skeptic cross-examination that 'sole architect' resume claim overstated role relative to teammate Priya's production implementation.

ownership_hiring_qa.gap_probed: freight-domain ramp-up vs experienced domain engineers
ownership_hiring_qa.response_summary: Asserter of fast ramp time based on structural similarity of previous work.
ownership_hiring_qa.response_quote: I move fast. I've built something structurally close to this already. I don't think I'd need much ramp time.

ownership_hiring_qa.response_summary: Acknowledges limited production incident volume due to Voltrix's small user base.
ownership_hiring_qa.response_quote: Fine, I've done on-call before. Though Voltrix's user base is still small, so I haven't seen serious incident volume yet.

ownership_hiring_qa.gap_probed: frequent job-hopping tenure pattern (3 jobs in 3.5 years)
ownership_hiring_qa.response_summary: Directly attributes frequent moves to pursuing better pay and title.
ownership_hiring_qa.response_quote: Better pay and title, mostly. Voltrix is more aligned with what I want long-term.
